stem:
Veena must measure $\angle PQR$ with a protractor.

Which plan measures the angle correctly?

options.text: Place the protractor on ray $PQ$ and read a scale mark, without putting the center on vertex $Q$.
Say that reading a degree number is what creates $\angle PQR$, instead of aligning the protractor to the arms.
Place the center on $Q$, align one arm with the zero-degree line, and read the scale reached by the other arm.
After reading $\angle PQR$, treat that same reading as also fixing every other unmarked angle at $Q$, beyond measuring these two arms.

teacher.key_rationale: To measure an angle, the protractor center sits on the vertex, one arm aligns with zero, and the other arm is read on the same scale. Skipping the center-on-vertex step, reversing reading and the angle, or stretching one reading to every angle at $Q$ all miss that plan.
